candidates.angle: Partha, son of Pritha, is the direct addressee
vyapashritya means taking refuge, and it is the single condition
Krishna lists the lowly born to show no one is barred
candidates.evidence: पापयोनयः, स्त्रियः, वैश्याः, तथा शूद्राः (born in difficult circumstances, and women, merchants, and workers)

en.intro: The Gita has been speaking of devotion and refuge. Now, listen closely to who exactly Krishna includes in that promise of the highest state.
en.notice: The verse lists women, merchants, and workers, and those born in difficult circumstances, to show that none of these birth or social categories bar the way. The word vyapashritya, having taken refuge, is the single condition that opens the highest state to all.
en.next: Krishna then asks what to speak of you, since even the most exalted have reached the same goal.
en.meaning: O Partha, even those born in difficult circumstances, and women, merchants, and workers, can reach the highest state by taking refuge in me.

hi.intro: गीता में भक्ति और शरण की बात हो रही है। अब सुनिए, कृष्ण उस सर्वोच्च लक्ष्य के लिए किसे-किसे शामिल करते हैं।
hi.meaning: हे पार्थ, जो पापयोनिवाले हों, स्त्रियाँ, वैश्य और शूद्र हों, वे भी मेरे शरण होकर परमगति को प्राप्त हो जाते हैं।
hi.notice: यह श्लोक स्त्रियों, वैश्यों और शूद्रों के साथ-साथ निम्न जन्म वालों को भी शामिल करता है, यह दिखाने के लिए कि कोई भी जन्म या सामाजिक स्थिति इस मार्ग में बाधा नहीं है। व्यपाश्रित्य, यानी शरण लेने का एक ही नियम, इस सर्वोच्च लक्ष्य के लिए सभी के द्वार खोल देता है।
hi.next: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि यदि शुद्ध ब्राह्मण और राजर्षि भी परमगति को प्राप्त होते हैं, तो तुम क्या कहोगे, इसलिए इस नश्वर लोक में मेरी पूजा करो।

issues: unsupported: "कृष्ण फिर पूछते हैं कि कोई उनकी पूजा करने से क्यों हिचकिचाए" (The next verse (verse 33) does not say Krishna asks why anyone would hesitate to worship him. Instead, it rhetorically asks, 'If even pure Brahmins and royal sages devoted to the divine reach the highest state, what to speak of you?' The script's notice about hesitation is unsupported.)
